newsitem.title: USA: SEC seeks comment on MSRB price reporting program.
newsitem.headline: SEC seeks comment on MSRB price reporting program.

text.p: The SEC said it will publish for comment next week an MSRB proposal that broker-dealers begin next year reporting prices and other data from muni trades with retail and institutional customers

The draft amendments to the Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board's rule G-14 would launch a major new phase in the board's transaction reporting program, which is designed to improve price transparency in the muni market.
The amendments, approved by the board last summer, would not take full effect until January 1, 1998, the MSRB notes in the introduction to the draft rule.
But MSRB asked SEC to approve the rule now so that firms will be ready for mandatory testing of the program next summer, Christopher Taylor, MSRB executive director, said in a telephone interview.
"This phase of transaction reporting will involve dealers having to make changes in their computer systems and internal procedures," Taylor said.
"We want to give the dealer community ample opportunity to begin to effect those changes so that this does not come as a surprise," Taylor said.
Under phase one of the program, dealers simply had to report data from interdealer trades, which they already provided to the National Securities Clearing Corporation.
The new rule would require each dealer to get an executing broker symbol from the National Association of Securities Dealers within 30 days of the the rule's final approval by SEC.

Each dealer would have to provide the Board by July 1, 1997 with the name and telephone number of a contact person responsible for testing the firm's ability to report customer transaction information, the draft rule says.

Dealers would test their reporting programs between July and December 1997 on a schedule to be announced by MSRB. They would begin reporting customer transactions fully on Jan. 1, 1998, the draft rule says.
The SEC said proposed rule G-14 will appear in the Federal Register sometime next week.
